name: Annalise Finch
note: Herald 24 Jan 2024, caption 'Elementary education major and Executive Vice President of SGA, Annalise Finch, takes a selfie with her class pet'. The caption is a clean identification but the photograph is useless as a portrait: she is standing on the dais with her back to the camera, arm raised holding the phone, and no part of her face is in the frame. Do not crop this one.

name: Antonina Clementi
note: Herald 21 April 2022, the WKU Forensics team championship photograph. Its caption does list every person by row and left-to-right position, and Clementi is named first in the front row, so this is one of the rare group frames that does identify people. It still cannot be used: the file the Herald published is download.png at 640x428 for about twenty-six people, so a single face is roughly a dozen pixels across and no larger version exists. The better-looking alternative, Herald 25 January 2023 ('Speaker of the Senate Julie Mishchuk (right) and Secretary of the Senate Antonina Clementi (left) pack up'), is also unusable: in that frame the left-hand figure is turned away with her head above the top edge, and the archive's existing portrait of Julie Mishchuk matches the right-hand woman, confirming Clementi is the one whose face is not in the picture.

name: Blake Graham
note: Two Herald frames name Blake Graham and neither shows his face. In the 23 September 2025 swearing-in the caption reads 'International Senator Grace Ekrikpo is sworn in by Chief Justice Blake Graham' but only one person is in the frame, the senator taking the oath, and that photograph has been used for Ekrikpo instead. In the 11 November 2025 frame, 'Chief Justice Blake Graham gives his final report as chief justice', the camera is behind him and he is the out-of-focus back of a head in the right foreground. The 11 November frame that introduces the two associate justices places Stirling and Hash by position but does not place Graham, so the third figure in it cannot be assumed to be him.

name: Emily Reinneck
note: Herald 19 August 2025, 'Soon to be Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee Chair Emily Reinneck is sworn in'. The caption names one person but the photograph is a mass swearing-in: three people on the right of the frame have their right hands raised taking the oath and a further row of people stands along the left wall. Nothing in the caption says which of them is Reinneck, so the frame identifies nobody. No other Herald photograph in the index names her.

name: Geoffrey Aberle
note: Herald 30 August 2023, 'Geoffrey Aberle is sworn in as a senator in the SGA chambers'. Two men are shaking hands after the oath. One has his back to the camera; the other faces us in an SGA polo shirt with a lanyard. The caption names only Aberle and says nothing about who is where, and the visible man could as easily be the officer who administered the oath. Compared against the archive's existing 2023-24 portraits (Romanov, Kurtz) and against Isaac King, the Chief Justice of that year, and he matches none of them, so the officer cannot be eliminated that way either. Same problem as the Cain Alvey election frame: no positions, so no identification.

name: Kayla Distler
note: Herald 13 April 2022, 'A petition regarding conditions in McLean Hall was started by WKU sophmore Kayla Distler'. The file is not a photograph of anyone: it is a screenshot of the Change.org petition page, showing the petition headline, a picture of McLean Hall and the signature count. The only image of a person on it is a thumbnail avatar about twenty pixels across beside the line naming her. Nothing to crop.

name: Jackson Smith
note: Herald 11 November 2025, 'Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee members Malachi Humble, Jackson Smith and Ciin Lun present a bill'. Three people at the lectern and the caption gives no positions. The archive's portrait of Ciin Lun does match the woman at the right, but that still leaves two men, and comparing the man in the white cap against the 24 February 2026 single-subject frame of Malachi Humble is not decisive either way: the beard and complexion do not clearly agree and the two views are a profile and a three-quarter. Same rule as the Mark Clark frame - a caption naming several people without saying who is where identifies nobody. Jackson Smith has no other captioned Herald photograph in the index.

name: MJ Mayo
note: Herald 25 September 2020, the SGA town hall debate. The caption names three people, Garrett Edmonds, MJ Mayo and Abbey Norvell, and gives no positions for any of them. The frame holds two people greeting each other on the stage, a man in a suit and a woman in a pale blazer, both in COVID face masks covering nose and mouth, so even the sexes of the three named do not narrow it. The same caption was uploaded three times in 2020 with different frames and none of them positions anybody.

name: Elias Thompson
note: Herald 1 October 2019, 'Elias Thompson, a WKU junior From Spring Hill, TN, and Julianna Low, a WKU sophomore from White House, TN, spent the morning of September 28 canvassing Bowling Green neighborhoods'. Two people are named and no positions are given, and in any case the photograph is made from behind: the one clear figure is walking away from the camera across a lawn with campaign literature and no face is visible. The second person is a sliver at the left edge.

name: Nicki Seay
note: Fell out of the photograph hunt rather than being looked for. The Herald's caption on the Downing Student Union opening of 26 August 2014 calls her 'Student Government Association President Nicki Seay'. The archive lists her only as Legislative Research chair in 2012-13 and Administrative Vice President in 2013-14, with nothing in 2014-15. Worth someone checking whether she held the presidency into the 2014-15 year, or succeeded to it late in 2013-14.

name: Beth McGrew
note: Herald 8 June 2015, 'WKU grad student Beth McGrew helps direct volunteer efforts during the Earth Day Garden Party ... sponsored by Project Grow and also the WKU Student Government Association'. The caption names one person, and the SGA sponsorship is a real tie, but the frame holds six or seven people at a garden bed and the caption gives no positions. Two women are standing; one of them has an arm outstretched, which is the only thing that looks like directing, and she is wearing a Project Grow T-shirt, which fits the event's other sponsor as easily as it fits McGrew. Her face is about a hundred pixels across. Not certain enough to cut.

name: Kaycee Gibson
note: Herald 6 March 2017, 'WKU graduate Kaycee Gibson (far right), 22, of Horse Cave, Ky. who is the volunteer coordinator'. The position is given, which is what makes this tempting, but the right-hand side of the frame holds two women rather than one: a fair-haired woman in focus at about x 1230-1330 and a second, dark-haired, at about x 1420-1490, half behind the pile of donated clothes at the very edge. Which of the two 'far right' means cannot be settled from the frame, and the second is too small and too occluded to cut in any case. The date is also a year after the 2015-16 term the archive lists her in, so there is no second line of evidence.

name: John Winstead
note: Herald, 3 September 2015 and twelve further uploads through September 2016, each captioned only 'John Winstead mug'. It is the columnist's mug for the Herald opinion column Synthesis. The column it first ran with, 'Uber and the neoliberalization of WKU', mentions SGA president Jay Todd Richey but says nothing about the columnist holding any office, and none of the thirteen captions does either. The only link to the archive's 2015-16 senator is the name, and a sitting senator writing an unsigned-interest opinion column would normally be disclosed. Not enough to cut a face on.

name: Julia Bright
note: Herald 14 September 2010, Constitution Week voter registration drive. Both the caption and the article identify her as president of the College Republicans, and the article quotes her in that capacity only: 'College Republicans President Julia Bright said several students registered'. Nothing in either mentions student government. The archive's Julia Bright served in 2007-08, three years earlier, and Bright is a common enough surname that a Louisville senior of the same name in 2010 is not an identification.

name: Joey Coe
note: Herald 10 December 2010, 'M is for Musician: Senior writing album for Honors thesis'. Single-subject frame and the caption names him, but neither caption nor article mentions student government: the piece is entirely about his music and his honours thesis. The archive lists Joey Coe as a senator in 2007-08 and Sustainability chair in 2008-09, two years before the photograph, so a Louisville senior of that name in December 2010 is consistent with him but is not evidence of it.

name: Chad Winston
note: Herald 3 February 2012, 'O is for Ordained: students use their voice for Christ'. The caption names him preaching at Cedar Grove Baptist Church and quotes him, but the article is about students who became ordained ministers and neither it nor the caption mentions student government. The photograph is a year after the 2010-11 term the archive lists him in, and there is no second line of evidence.

name: Chris Jankowski
note: Herald 7 December 2010, resident assistants making signs in Pearce-Ford Tower. The caption names three people, Laqisha Walton, Chris Jankowski and Matt Brockman, and gives no positions. Three people are in the frame: a woman kneeling at the left, who is Walton by elimination, and two men, one bending over the banner and one seated at the right. Nothing in the caption or the article separates Jankowski from Brockman.

name: Courtney Hamilton
note: Herald 9 October 2014, 'Owensboro junior Courtney Hamilton and Louisville junior Emily Woodruff are residents in the newly constructed Kentucky Street Apartments'. The caption names two women and gives no positions, and only one person is visible anywhere in the frame, standing at the right of a kitchen. There is no way to tell whether the woman shown is Hamilton or Woodruff. The same caption was uploaded three times in October 2014 with the same problem.

name: Katie Martin
note: Herald 9 April 2013, 'Bowling Green junior Keyana Boka hugs Campbellsville graduate student Katie Martin after finding out she will remain SGA president'. Two women are embracing and the caption gives no positions, but it resolves the wrong way: the one facing the camera is Keyana Boka, whose face the archive already holds in the portrait cut from this very frame and filed as 2013-14-keyanna-boka.jpg, and who also matches the separate Boka portrait of 31 October 2013. Martin is therefore the blonde woman with her back to the camera, and none of her face is in the picture.

name: Taylor Ruby
note: Herald 15 April 2014, the Fiji house clean-up. The caption names three men, Braden Proffitt, Taylor Ruby and Zack Van Zant, and gives no positions. Three men are in the frame, all young, all in short sleeves, and nothing in the caption or the article separates them.

name: William Berry
note: Herald 2 December 2014, the self-defence class. The caption names two men, Desmond Hutchison and William Berry, and gives no positions. Both are on the mat mid-hold with their faces turned into each other's shoulders, and further pairs are grappling in the background, so even if the caption placed them there would be no usable face to cut.

name: Maggie Phelps
note: Herald 28 April 2026, 'New Judicial Council member Maggie Phelps speaks with fellow judicial council members as they prepare to vote for the new Senate speaker'. The caption is an outright SGA identification but names no positions, and three young women are crowded together in the frame, one of them with her back to the camera. Nothing separates Phelps from the other two council members. Her only other captioned frame in the index is the Herald's own news-staff mug of 1 September 2023, which is a single subject but ties her to the newspaper rather than to student government.

name: Blake Bowden
note: Herald 27 November 2017, from the photo gallery 'The evolution of black hair'. Single subject and a good frame, but neither the caption nor the gallery mentions student government: the whole piece is about his hair and about workplace discrimination, and the caption gives only his name, age and home town. The photograph is also from the academic year after the 2016-17 term the archive lists him in. Name and timing alone are not an identification.

name: Troy Davis
note: Herald 6 March 2018, republished from 30 April 2013: 'Louisville senior Troy Davis and Louisville freshman Hunter Heath celebrate after Delta Tau Delta wins Tug on April 29, 2013'. Two people are named with no positions and half a dozen men are cheering in the frame. Worse, the archive's Troy Davis is a senator in 2020-21, and a Louisville senior of 2013 would have graduated seven years earlier. Almost certainly a different man.

name: John May
note: Herald 22 March 2021. The lead is a plain false positive: the caption reads 'John Mayer's new album is complete' and the file is attached to an item about the musician John Mayer, not about anyone at WKU. The only other match in the photograph index is a 2023 concert caption about a singer named John Sutphin. Nothing to do with the archive's 2018-19 senator.

name: Avery Wells
note: Herald 2 February 2022, 'WKU cheerleader Avery Wells laughs as he cheers on the Hilltoppers during a basketball game'. Neither this nor his two later frames, at the 2024 Homecoming Step Show with Phi Beta Sigma, mentions student government, and all three are after the 2020-21 term the archive lists him in. A common name with no SGA tie in any caption.

name: Brian Anderson
note: Ruled a false positive before this pass and left rejected. The leads file frame, Herald 10 February 2015, is 'Brian Anderson, a senior from LaRue County High School, poses for a portrait ... Anderson has just signed with WKU for the forensics speech and debate team', which says nothing about student government. Recorded for whoever looks next: there is a second frame, Herald 2 November 2016, captioned 'Donald Trump surrogate Brian Anderson, sophomore from Hodgenville, watches Hillary Clinton surrogate Lily Nellans, junior from Des Moines, Iowa, answer questions'. Hodgenville is the county seat of LaRue County, so the two frames are consistent with one man who came to WKU on the forensics team and was a sophomore in November 2016, which is the year the archive makes him Legislative Research chair. It is still only a name plus timing, the 2016 frame names two people and positions neither, and Brian Anderson is a common name. Not enough to overturn the rejection, but the second frame should be on the record.
